3.translation: and proclaim the greatness of your Lord,

5.footnotes: [2] And other sins and bad conducts and morals.

6.translation: and do not do a favor for a greater return[3],
6.footnotes: [3] Or: do not consider your good deeds as a favor to Allah, thinking of your little deeds as abundant.

7.translation: and be patient for the sake of your Lord.

8.footnotes: [4] For the second time, causing all to rise from the dead for resurrection. See 39:68.

9.translation: that Day will be a difficult day,

11.translation: Leave me to deal with the one whom I created lonely[5],
11.footnotes: [5] i.e., having no wealth or children. It refers to al-Walīd bin al-Mughīrah, who was impressed by the Qur’an, yet he publicly denied it to win the approval of the pagans of Makkah.

14.translation: and gave him a life of comfort and power,

15.translation: yet he aspires that I should give him more.

16.translation: By no means! For he has been stubborn against Our verses.

17.translation: I will subject him to an unbearable punishment.

18.translation: For he reflected and plotted [against the Qur’an][6].

19.translation: May he perish, how he plotted!

20.translation: Again, may he perish, how he plotted!

24.translation: then said, “This is nothing but magic from the past.

25.translation: This is nothing but the words of a man.”

26.translation: Soon I will make him burn in the Scorching Fire[7].
26.footnotes: [7] "Saqar" is one of the names of Hell.

27.translation: How do you know what Scorching Fire is?

28.translation: It leaves nothing and spares no one,

31.translation: We have only appointed angels as keepers of the Fire, and We have only made their number as a test for the disbelievers[8], so that those who were given the Scripture may have certainty and the believers may increase in faith; and neither those who were given the Scripture nor the believers may have any doubts; and so that those [hypocrites] in whose hearts is sickness and the disbelievers may say, “What does Allah mean by this number?” Thus Allah causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and none knows the soldiers of your Lord but He. This is but a reminder to mankind.
31.footnotes: [8] To say what they want to say, so their punishment will be multiplied for them. Abu Jahl, one of the chief pagans in Makkah, made fun of the Prophet (ﷺ) when they came to know that the keepers of Hell are nineteen angels, so he ridiculed this number and said that it is an easy number to overcome.

33.translation: and by the night when it departs,

34.translation: and by the dawn when it brightens,

35.translation: Hellfire is indeed one of the greatest matters,

37.translation: to whoever among you chooses to advance or regress.

38.translation: Every soul is held in pledge[9] for its deeds,

39.translation: except the People of the Right[10],
39.footnotes: [10] i.e., the believers who receive their records of deeds in their right hands.

40.translation: who will be in gardens, asking one another

43.translation: They will say, “We were not among those who prayed,

44.translation: nor did we feed the poor,

45.translation: and we indulged in falsehood along with those who indulged in it,

46.translation: and we denied the Day of Judgment,

47.translation: until the certainty [of death] came to us.”

48.translation: So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.

49.translation: Then what is the matter with them that they turn away from the Reminder,

50.translation: as if they were terrified wild asses,

52.translation: In fact, each one of them desires that open [divine] letters be sent to each of them[11].
52.footnotes: [11] Instead of Muhammad (ﷺ), not due to the lack of proofs or signs presented to them but out of obstinacy and arrogance.

53.translation: By no means! They rather do not fear the Hereafter.

54.translation: No indeed! This [Qur’an] is a reminder.

55.translation: So whoever wills may take heed.

56.translation: But they will not take heed unless Allah so wills. He is most worthy to be feared and most worthy to forgive.
